text:
Mia: Heads up — bringing up zephyr-lite-v2 (Llama->Mistral hybrid) on staging. After INT4 quant we see a reproducible long-context summarization drift; ROUGE-L down ~6 pts vs fp16 baseline. Not a single prompt fluke.
Sam: Can you paste the failing prompt + outputs? I suspect the fft-based rotary canonicalization change from the quant PR might have shifted phases.
Mia: Prompt and outputs below. First block is fp16, second is int4 q8_0 baseline from the pipeline.
```
PROMPT: "Summarize the following meeting notes into 5 bullets... [long 3k token context]
FP16: 1) action items..., 2) timeline..., 3) risks..., 4) owners..., 5) next steps.
INT4: 1) timeline..., 2) risks..., 3) random repetition, 4) missing owners, 5) extraneous filler.
```
Mia: Also saw odd token-level logit swings early in generation (first 40 tokens).
Anita: Running quick bisect across quant commits now. Early result: commit f3a2b4..f3a2ff includes "fft-rotary-phase-simplify" and correlates with BLEU/ROUGE drop on our sanity set. Bisect command I used: `git bisect run ./scripts/eval_small.sh zephyr-lite-v2` — reproduces in ~6 runs.
Sam: Ok that's useful. Could be that the FFT canonicalization changed per-head phase normalization (headwise vs shared). If per-head scaling changed, kv-cache alignment could drift.
Leo: Tokenizer check: I compared token ids around sentinels and patched BOS handling earlier this week. Unlikely but let's diff token ids for the failing context: `python -c "import tkn; print(tkn.encode_long(ctx)[:120])"` — can you dump the ids?
Mia: Pasted token ids to the thread (trimmed). No obvious off-by-one but I did notice a repeating subsequence when token id 5027 occurs — looks like a subtoken boundary aliasing case.
Anita: I ran a quick local inference with kv-cache disabled and single-request unbatched; the regression shrinks to ~1.2 ROUGE pts. With kv-cache enabled it's the full -6pts. So kv-cache + fft-rotary interaction seems real.
Sam: That strongly suggests rotation phase canonicalization mismatch between encoder pattern used for cache keys and live generation path. Two candidates: 1) kernel phase normalization (fft->real reorder) 2) per-head packing order change during quant kernel lowering.
Anita: Quick log from the runtime when running int4 (abridged):
```
[INF] kv_cache: store key shape (12, 128, 64)
[INF] rotary_phase: applied headwise scale 0.9875
[WRN] rotary_phase: canonicalize path used fallback fft_real for heads 4..7
```
Anita: Notice the fallback message — our runtime falls back to a slower canonicalize path for some heads under int4, due to alignment constraints.
Leo: If some heads used fallback codepath then the phase basis could differ subtly (ordering/stride changes). That'll definitely skew cached key alignment.
Sam: Plan suggestion: 1) patch runtime to enforce identical canonicalization path for cache write/read (even if slower) for correctness in the short term; 2) re-run quant calibrations and INT4 eval; 3) add unit test that simulates mixed canonicalize paths.
Mia: Sounds good. Anita can you try the runtime patch and post quick numbers? If it recovers, we push a hotfix to staging and rerun full eval.
Anita: On it. Running a patched build now. Quick local numbers show ROUGE-L back within 0.8 pts of fp16 after forcing canonical path equality. Pushed a build to staging: `staging://zephyr-lite-v2/1779993500`
Deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Staging deploy completed for zephyr-lite-v2 @ build 1779993500 — https://staging.redwood/zephyr-lite-v2/1779993500 :rocket:
Mia: Great. Next steps: Anita will run full eval overnight, Sam will run tokenized logit drift script and add regression alert, Leo will add a tokenizer shadowing test. I'll open an RFC to make the canonicalization deterministic across quant lowering.
Sam: I'll also add a perf note — keeping canonicalization identical will cost ~3-6% token throughput in INT4 for affected shapes; need to weigh perf vs correctness for now.
Mia: OK let's treat correctness first for the release. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Leo: ack :eyes:
Anita: assigning follow-ups in the ticket.
